head: 0098ee939e2d701ca3085c9e8e2fe3003a907836
summary: Fixed O-020 (M2) in eng/rules-parity.ps1. Read-Entries now refuses any dash at column 0 to 2 that does not carry `name:` on the same line, using the regex `^ {0,2}-(\s|$)` the decision specified. So a bare `  -` line with `name:` on the next line exits 2 with its file:line instead of being skipped or folded into the entry above it. List items sit at 4 or 6 spaces and never match. Three rows were added to C-005 in tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1, each requiring CANNOT-READ at the dash line under both powershell.exe and pwsh: a bare-dash entry first after `rules:`, one just above the settled marker, and one at column 0. On a copy with the first shape, the committed reader said AGREE (exit 0) and the fixed reader says CANNOT-READ at fitness.yaml:72. The regressions pass: C-001 to C-005, C-007 and the 8 rule Facts.

files.why: O-020/M2: the entry refusal regex is now `^ {0,2}-(\s|$)` (was `^  -\s`), so an entry opened by a bare dash at column 0 to 2 exits 2 with file:line instead of being missed.

O-020: three C-005 rows (a bare-dash entry first after rules:, one just above the settled marker, one at column 0), each requiring CANNOT-READ at the dash line under both shells. Get-LineOf gained an -Exact switch to locate the bare dash line.

obligations.how: The refusal at eng/rules-parity.ps1 is now `^ {0,2}-(\s|$)`, the wider form the decision chose over the reviewer's. C-005 now feeds a `  -` / `    name: 'AYamlOnlyRule (*.cs)'` entry first after `rules:`, the same just above '# settled by SL-023', and a column-0 `-` variant. Each exits 2 with "CANNOT-READ .taad/fitness.yaml:<dash line>: an entry that does not start with 'name:' on its dash line" under powershell.exe and pwsh (12/12 checks). The committed reader gave AGREE, exit 0, on the first shape.

Owed to validate-slice, and not changed this attempt. Attempt 1 ran the full harness three times with the same verdict for every row. This fix only touches the parity yaml reader's entry refusal; the C-007 clean scenario (the harness runs parity first) still passes.
Owed to validate-slice, and unchanged since attempt 1. The harness checks the folder listing after the two-step rename before trusting D3/D4/D9 (C-012).
Owed to validate-slice, and unchanged since attempt 1. C-014 flips D13's recorded outcome and the harness exits 1 with DIVERGENCE-CLOSED.

tests.command: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1 -Case C-001 (and C-002, C-003, C-004)

tests.note: The harness runs parity first; the clean scenario is still CLEAN, and the stray-hit bite still exits 2. All checks held.

follow_ups: Two review laps (M1, M2) each found a YAML spelling that the line reader neither read nor refused. Other legal spellings may still slip past it: flow mappings (`  - {name: ...}`), anchors and aliases, a `name:` key written as `? name`, and tabs. It may be worth one more look to enumerate them, or a cross-check against a count of entries from the engine where the TAAD engine is present (harness step 1 already compares Fitness's rule count with twinned + settled on the clean scenario).
